Visit note | 2025-12-18 03:00 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Wasim Uddin, 65, male. Mr. Uddin presents complaining of a red eye, sticky yellow discharge, and eyelids stuck together in the morning. He states this started during an outbreak at an office in Old Dhaka. He works as a farmer and has a history of Bronchial asthma. He denies any recent eye trauma, changes in vision, or pain moving the eye. On examination: visual acuity 6/9 in the right eye, BP 131/86 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 78 kg. The conjunctiva is injected with purulent discharge; cornea is clear. Assessment: Bacterial conjunctivitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to wash hands often, do not share towels, and stay away from work for two days. Follow-up in 1 week if not better.

Visit note | 2025-12-18 03:00 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Eva Dewan, 48, female. Mrs. Dewan reports thick white discharge and itching in the vaginal area. She mentions these complaints began during the humid monsoon in Kamrangirchar. She is employed as a hotel receptionist and has a background of Bronchial asthma. She denies pelvic pain, urinary symptoms, or bleeding. On examination: random blood glucose 6.9 mmol/L, BP 113/80 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 79 kg. Speculum examination shows thick curd-like discharge and mucosal erythema. Assessment: Vulvovaginal candidiasis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to wear cotton underwear, avoid scented soaps, and keep the area dry. Follow-up in 2 weeks if it does not clear.

Visit note | 2025-12-18 04:00 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Eva Khatun, 52, female. Ms. Khatun describes a coated tongue, dull discomfort in the belly, and a fever that climbs a little higher every day for over a week. She notes that her illness began a few days after eating street food at a fair in Mirpur. She works as a restaurant cook and has no known comorbidities. She denies vomiting, diarrhea, or shortness of breath. On examination: temperature 101.5°F, BP 133/70 mmHg, pulse 105 bpm, weight 79 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild right upper quadrant tenderness; no organomegaly. Assessment: Typhoid fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat soft home-cooked food, drink boiled or bottled water only, and avoid street food. Follow-up in 7 days with a repeat blood count.

Visit note | 2025-12-18 04:00 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Khadija Miah, 46, female. Mrs. Miah complains of an itch that is worse in humid weather along with a ring-shaped itchy red rash. She states it began during the humid monsoon in Shyamoli. Visit note | 2025-12-20 09:30 AM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Saiful Pramanik, 19, male. Mr. Pramanik comes to the clinic reporting a mild wheeze, no high fever, and a persistent cough that has lingered for one to two weeks after a cold. He notes that the trouble started after a dusty road trip to Motijheel. He works as a garment factory worker and has no prior chronic medical history. He denies any night sweats, chest pain, or significant weight loss, though he notes some throat irritation when breathing cold air in the mornings. On physical examination, his temperature is recorded at 99.6°F, blood pressure is 112/84 mmHg, pulse is 86 beats per minute, oxygen saturation stands at 97% on room air, and his weight is 89 kg. Chest examination reveals normal vesicular breathing with occasional scattered expiratory wheezes, but no dullness to percussion or signs of respiratory distress. Upper airway examination shows mild pharyngeal congestion without tonsillar exudate. Assessment: Acute bronchitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink warm fluids, use steam inhalation twice daily, and avoid exposure to smoke. Follow-up in 2 weeks if the cough continues.
